course_title: Psychology of Sport, Physical Activity and Health
course_description:
Introduction to the impact of psychological variables on participation and performance in sport and exercise and the influence of participation in sport and exercise on the psychological characteristics of the individual.

Psychology is the scientific study of how people think, feel, behave, and interact with their environments. PSYC2000 introduces students to key topics in sport, exercise, and health psychology while examining the theories, concepts, and evidence that inform contemporary practice. Throughout the course, students will explore psychological factors that influence performance, participation, and wellbeing, as well as the ways in which participation in sport and physical activity shapes psychological functioning.

Rather than focusing on a single way of understanding behaviour, the course introduces multiple theoretical perspectives—including mainstream psychological approaches and contemporary transactional and ecological perspectives—to help students appreciate the strengths and limitations of different explanations of human behaviour. Across the semester, students will examine motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes, and consider how these interact within complex sport, exercise, and health environments.

The course combines self-paced online lectures with interactive, in-person workshops to create diverse learning opportunities. The online lectures provide the theoretical foundations and research evidence, while the embodied, collaborative, and multimodal workshops emphasise active learning through movement, problem-solving, reflection, and real-life application. Together, these complementary learning experiences prepare students to apply psychological principles to sport, physical activity, health, and performance contexts.

PSYC2000 builds upon foundational knowledge developed in SPCG1000, PSYC1020, and PSYC1030 and places a strong emphasis on critical thinking, evidence-informed practice, and the integration of theory with practice.

course_aims:
This course explores the psychological processes that influence performance, participation, and wellbeing in sport, physical activity, and health. It aims to introduce students to key topics such as motivation, cognition, emotion, leadership, and social processes, while examining how participation in sport and physical activity can, in turn, shape psychological functioning and human behaviour.

Drawing on multiple theoretical perspectives, ranging from traditional psychological approaches to contemporary transactional and ecological perspectives, students will develop a deeper understanding of human behaviour as emerging through dynamic interactions between individuals and their physical and social environments. Throughout the course, students will critically evaluate theory and evidence and learn to apply psychological concepts to authentic sport, physical activity, and health contexts.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how psychological variables influence participation and performance in sport and exercise settings.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how participation in sport and exercise influences the psychological characteristics of the individual player/participant.
Demonstrate applied knowledge about sport and exercise psychology as a practitioner (e.g., scientist, coach, HPE teacher, fitness instructor, athlete and/or exerciser).
Retrieve and critically review information relevant to topics of research in sport and exercise psychology.
Experience a general introduction to the research process in sport and exercise psychology through learning how to critique the literature.
Work effectively within a team in order to develop communication and process management skills, and facilitate peer-assisted, collaborative learning.

assessment_details.title: Creative Motivation Timeline (Individual)
assessment_details.task_description: Objectives Apply psychological theories of motivation to an authentic personal experience. Critically reflect on the dynamic interactions between the individual, the task, and the environment. Develop evidence-informed strategies to support ongoing motivation and behaviour change. Integrate theory, research, and lived experience through creative communication. Description Working in teams of four to five students, each group will identify a shared sport, physical activity, or health-related goal to pursue over an eight-week period (Weeks 4–11). Midway through this journey (end of Week 8), each student will individually submit a Creative Motivation Timeline illustrating their own motivational journey. The timeline will be organised around three phases—past, present, and future. Students will creatively represent where they were at the beginning of the journey, where they are midway through, and where they hope to be by the end of the project. Throughout each phase, students will reflect on themselves, the task, and their environment, drawing on psychological theories and concepts studied in class to explain how these interacting factors have shaped their motivation over time. Rather than presenting motivation as something fixed, students are encouraged to illustrate its dynamic and evolving nature. They should identify key moments, challenges, turning points, and adaptations that influenced their journey, critically evaluating the strategies that have supported or hindered their progress. Building on these reflections, students will develop an evidence-informed action plan for the second half of the project. The submission should take the form of a creative artefact that visually communicates the complexity of their motivational journey while integrating psychological theory and research. Students are encouraged to use timelines, diagrams, illustrations, photographs, symbols, or other creative approaches that best represent their experience. The emphasis of this assessment is on thoughtful integration rather than description. Students are expected to critically connect course concepts to their own experiences, demonstrating how psychological theory can help explain, interpret, and improve real-world behaviour. assessment_details.title: Goal Journey Portfolio (Group)
assessment_details.task_description: Objectives Apply psychological theories and concepts to an authentic sport, physical activity, or health experience. Integrate knowledge from motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes to understand behaviour from multiple psychological perspectives. Develop collaborative problem-solving, critical reflection, and evidence-informed practice. Communicate learning creatively through a multimodal portfolio. Description Working in small groups, students will identify a shared sport, physical activity, or health-related goal and pursue it over an eight-week period (Weeks 4–11). Throughout their journey, students will document their experiences using a range of evidence and multimodal representations, such as photographs, videos, reflections, observations, performance data, creative artefacts, or other forms of documentation that best capture their learning and experiences. The portfolio will be organised around the four core themes of the course—motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes. For each section, students will critically reflect on their experiences by integrating relevant psychological theories and concepts explored throughout the semester. Students will be encouraged to compare different theoretical perspectives, including mainstream and transactional approaches, and evaluate how each contributes to understanding behaviour, performance, participation, and wellbeing. The final portfolio will be presented as a digital artefact (e.g., PowerPoint, Canva, or another approved digital platform) that creatively communicates the group's journey while demonstrating the application of psychological theory to authentic, lived experiences. The emphasis of this assessment is not simply on achieving the goal itself, but on thoughtfully documenting, analysing, and reflecting on the psychological processes that emerged throughout the journey. learning_activities.topic: Introduction: Why Theory Matters – Four Ways of Understanding Sport, Exercise, and Health Behaviour Online lecture: This week introduces the course and explores four major metatheoretical perspectives that shape how we understand behaviour in sport, physical activity, and health. Students will discover how different theoretical lenses lead to different research questions, interventions, and professional practices, providing the conceptual foundation for the rest of the course. In-Person Workshop – Experiencing Theory Through the Body In this first interactive workshop, students will engage in embodied, collaborative, and multimodal learning activities designed to experience the main theoretical perspectives of this course rather than simply learn about them. Through movement, discussion, and creative problem-solving, students will begin developing the systems thinking that underpins the course. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

Understanding Motivation and Goal Setting Online lectures: This week examines why people participate and persist in sport and physical activity through major theories of motivation. Students will explore evidence-based goal-setting strategies and consider how goals can be used to support motivation, performance, and wellbeing. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Motivation from a Transactional Perspective Online Lecture: The goal of week 3 is to introduce motivation as something that emerges through the ongoing interaction between individuals and their environments. Students will explore how affordances and learning environments can shape motivation, engagement, and lifelong participation in physical activity. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Workshop: Solving the Motivation Challenge In-Person Workshop: This embodied and interactive workshop challenges students to address one of the biggest questions in sport, exercise, and health psychology: How do we help people move towards more active and healthier lifestyles? Through collaborative, multimodal problem-solving activities, students will apply motivational theories to design creative, evidence-informed solutions for real-world behavioural challenges. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

Cognition in Sport and Physical Activity Online Lectures: This week explores the reciprocal relationship between cognition, physical activity, and sport. Students will first examine how physical activity influences executive functions and cognitive development before exploring how athletes perceive information, allocate attention, make decisions, and develop expertise in dynamic sporting environments. Contemporary approaches to perceptual-cognitive training and emerging technologies will be critically evaluated, encouraging students to consider not only their potential benefits but also whether improvements meaningfully transfer to performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Decision Making: A Transactional Perspective Online Lecture: This week introduces an ecological dynamics perspective on decision making, challenging traditional views of cognition as an internal process. Students will explore how decisions emerge through continuous interactions between the individual, the task, and the environment, and consider how practice environments can be designed to support adaptive behaviour. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Workshop: Designing Enriched Environments for Cognition In-Person Workshop : This practical workshop takes place in the gym, where students will experience how movement can be intentionally designed to stimulate cognition and support whole-person development. Through embodied experimentation, students will learn how to create enriched physical activity environments that promote attention, adaptability, creativity, and decision making. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

Understanding Emotion in Sport and Physical Activity Online Lecture: This week introduces major theories of emotion and examines on one hand, how emotions influence performance, participation, and wellbeing, and on the other hand, physical activity and sport participation influence emotional states. Students will explore practical strategies for recognising and using emotions effectively in sport and physical activity. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Adaptation from a Transactional Perspective Online lecture: The goal of this week is to explore emotion as a dynamic process emerging through interactions between the individual and their environment. Students will examine how appropriately designed challenges can foster adaptive emotional states and resilience in sport and physical activity, including contemporary transactional approaches to psychological adaptation. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Social Relationships in Sport and Physical Activity Online Lecture: This week explores how relationships with coaches, teammates, parents, peers, and other social agents shape development, performance, and mental health. Students will examine the importance of creating supportive, psychologically safe, and developmentally appropriate sport and physical activity environments. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Workshop: Emotion as an Embodied and Transactional Process In-Person Workshop: This embodied workshop concludes the emotion module by inviting students to discover how emotions are experienced, expressed, and regulated through the body and movement. Through interactive and reflective activities, students will learn to design physical activity experiences that embrace a truly holistic understanding of human functioning. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

Leadership Online Lecture: This week examines leadership in sport, exercise, and health settings. Students will explore different leadership approaches and consider how effective leaders influence motivation, team functioning, wellbeing, and performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Workshop: Integrating Psychology into Practice In-Person Workshop: In the final workshop, students will integrate concepts from across the course through embodied, interactive, and reflective learning experiences. Drawing together motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes, students will design and evaluate holistic approaches to supporting performance, participation, health, and wellbeing in real-world contexts. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06
